a short DNA motif located at the 3' end of the spacer affects the acquisition efficiency of a spacer and that the position of this motif with respect to 5'-AAG is important to its effect.
the first base of a protospacer, the protospacer-adjacent motif, and the 3′-AA of a spacer affect acquisition efficiency into the type I Escherichia CRISPR array.
the efficiency of spacer integration into the CRISPCR array is affected by the protospacer-adjacent motif and the 3′ dinucleotide of the protospacers.

a novel mechanism that affects the efficiency of spacer adaptation into the CRISPER array.
the mechanism that determines the efficiency of spacer integration into a bacterial genome.
the mechanisms that govern adaptation into CRISPR arrays.

the CRISPR-Cas system has evolved a mechanism to recognize the 5′ end of the protospacers, which is essential for adaptation.
a spacer is acquired into a CRISPR array if the protospacer has the 5′ AAG motif and if the 3′-AA dinucleotide is present in a spacer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a motif that affects the efficiency of acquisition of spacers into the CRISCR array of Escherichia col.
the CRISPR adaptation process is a complex and highly regulated mechanism that is influenced by the sequence of the spacers and the protospacer.
the efficiency of spacer adaptation is affected by a combination of several factors, including the presence of the PAM, the 3′-AA motif, and the first nucleotide of the spacer.

the CRISPR adaptation process can be modulated in vivo and that this modulation can be used for engineering of the CRISPR arrays.
